_about: How the third-party lens names a party that has no stored Organization. Such a party is named by the registrable domain of the name it was reached through, so a provider that spreads its service across many registrable domains shows up once per domain. A name group gives those domains one vendor name: pattern is a regular expression matched against the whole registrable domain, and source is the provider's own documentation of the names it uses. reverse_zones are the DNS zones of reverse lookups; a name in them is an address's pointer, not a vendor. Add groups here, not in Go code. reserved_zones are special-use top-level domains (RFC 2606, RFC 6761, RFC 6762) whose names reach no one, such as msv1.invalid; a party is never named by one.
